name: Process one business customer order from order receipt to cash (order to cash)
function: finance and sales operations: order to cash
summary: Order to cash turns a business customer's purchase order into goods shipped, an invoice and cash in the bank. Customer service keys or imports the order, the ERP checks price, stock and credit, and about one order in eight stops for a credit analyst. After the warehouse ships, a nightly run invoices the customer, who pays on its own schedule; about half of invoices are paid late and go through reminders and collector calls. Cash application matches payments to invoices, and short payments become deductions that analysts research with sales before a credit memo or a repayment closes them. Almost all elapsed time is the customer's payment term and delay.

baseline.org_archetype: A US mid-size manufacturer or distributor selling on net 30 credit terms to business customers, with an ERP, EDI with larger customers, a warehouse management system and a bank lockbox.
baseline.notes: One order is assumed to produce one shipment and one invoice. Returns, rebates and customer master maintenance are separate processes.

unit_of_work: one business customer order (one shipment and one invoice)
trigger: A business customer sends a purchase order by EDI, email, phone or fax.
end_state: The invoice is fully paid and the cash applied, or closed by credit memo or write-off, or the order is cancelled or declined before shipping.

volume.seasonality: Higher before quarter-end and in the customer's peak season; lower in late December.

evidence.note: Author estimate for a company of about $500 million revenue with an average order of about $8,000.

triggered_by.from: Sales representatives entering orders taken in person

produces.object: revenue, receivable, cash and bad debt postings
deduction root causes and credit memos

systems.name: ERP order management, billing and receivables modules
EDI translator (850 orders, 855 acknowledgements, 810 invoices, 820 remittances)
Email and shared order and AR mailboxes
Customer supplier portals (e-invoicing and AP portals run by customers)
Bank lockbox and cash reporting portal
Proof of delivery and document archive

steps.name: Log incoming order
steps.description: Orders arrive as EDI purchase orders that the translator imports straight into the ERP, or as emailed PDF purchase orders, phone calls and faxes that land in the customer service queue. The system time-stamps each order and routes manual ones to the order entry queue.
outputs: order in ERP or in order entry queue

next.condition: email, phone or fax order needs keying

evidence.note: Order channels described by wiki_o2c. The 35 percent EDI share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Key order into ERP
steps.description: The customer service representative opens the customer's purchase order, finds the customer and ship-to in the ERP, keys each item, quantity, requested date and the customer PO number, and checks the price the customer quoted against the contract or price list.

error.defect_description: Wrong item, quantity, price, ship-to or customer PO number keyed

evidence.note: Order capture and validation described by emagia_o2c. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Check price and availability
steps.description: The ERP prices each line from the customer's contract or price list, compares it with any price on the customer PO, and checks available-to-promise stock for the requested date. Lines priced differently from the customer PO are flagged.

next.condition: customer PO price differs from system price

evidence.note: Standard ERP pricing and availability check; mismatch share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Confirm price with sales
steps.description: The sales rep gets an email from customer service showing the system price and the customer's price, checks the latest quote or agreement, and either approves a price override within their authority or asks the customer to accept the correct price.

error.defect_description: Override approved at a price that does not match the agreement

control.basis: Pricing authority policy: price overrides below list or contract need sales approval within set limits

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Run automated credit check
steps.description: When the order is saved the ERP adds its value to the customer's open receivables and open orders, compares the total with the credit limit, and checks for past-due balances or a credit hold flag. Orders that fail are blocked from release.
inputs: customer credit limit and AR balance

control.basis: Credit policy: orders over the credit limit or with past-due balances are blocked until credit releases them

next.condition: within limit and no past-due flag
new customer without a credit account

evidence.note: Credit check and order holds described by emagia_o2c; PCF 9.2.1.5 review existing accounts. Block rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Review credit-blocked order
steps.description: The credit analyst opens the blocked order list, reviews the customer's aging, payment history and any payment in transit, checks with the collector or sales rep, and releases the order, holds it until the customer pays, or escalates it to the credit manager.

error.defect_description: Order released to a customer about to default

next.condition: held until customer pays past-due balance or prepays

evidence.note: PCF 9.2.1.7 reinstate or suspend accounts based on credit policies. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Set up new customer credit account
steps.description: The credit analyst sends a credit application, collects trade and bank references and the customer's tax exemption certificate, pulls a business credit report, screens the customer against the OFAC sanctions list and recommends a credit limit and terms.
outputs: new customer account with recommended limit

error.defect_description: Limit set too high from incomplete references

control.basis: OFAC sanctions regulations (31 CFR chapter V): US persons may not deal with blocked persons, so new customers are screened against the SDN list

evidence.note: PCF 9.2.1.2 analyze and approve new account applications; OFAC obligation from ofac_faq. APQC median credit approval cycle is 5 calendar days (cfo_credit); the wait here plus the approval step is set to match.

steps.name: Approve credit limit or override
steps.description: The credit manager reviews the analyst's recommendation or escalation, the credit report and the order value, and approves the limit or a one-time override, requires prepayment or a guarantee, or declines. A declined applicant is told the decision.
outputs: approved limit, override, prepayment requirement or decline

control.basis: Equal Credit Opportunity Act, Regulation B (12 CFR 1002.9(a)(3)): trade credit applicants must be told of the action taken within a reasonable time

evidence.note: Notification rule from cfpb_regb; approval queues named as a cause of slow credit approval (cfo_credit). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Wait for customer payment or prepayment
steps.description: The customer is asked to pay the past-due balance, send a prepayment or provide a guarantee before the order ships. The order stays blocked while the customer's AP team arranges payment.

next.condition: customer does not pay; order cancelled

evidence.note: Customer response time and cancellation share are author estimates; external hands-on time is not counted.

steps.name: Acknowledge order and release to warehouse
steps.description: The ERP sends an order acknowledgement by EDI or email with the confirmed ship date and releases the order to the warehouse management system in the next wave release.

evidence.note: Confirmation then fulfilment (wiki_o2c). Wave timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Pick, pack and stage order
steps.description: A warehouse associate picks the lines with an RF scanner, packs and labels the cartons or builds the pallet, and stages it at the dock for the carrier. Short picks are reported to customer service.

evidence.note: Pick and pack time per B2B order and short-pick share are author estimates; this labour is often counted in a separate fulfilment process.

steps.name: Notify customer of backorder
steps.description: Customer service sees the short pick, checks the expected replenishment date and emails or calls the customer to ask whether to ship what is available and backorder the rest or hold the order until complete.

next.condition: customer waits for stock; re-picked when it arrives

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Confirm shipment in ERP
steps.description: The shipping clerk weighs the shipment, books the carrier, prints the bill of lading and packing list, and confirms the shipment in the WMS so the ERP posts the goods issue with the carrier tracking number.

error.defect_description: Shipment confirmed with wrong quantity or date

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Generate invoice in billing run
steps.description: The nightly billing run creates an invoice for each shipped order from the goods issue, with prices, freight and sales tax, posts the receivable and revenue, and sends clean invoices by EDI or email. Orders with billing blocks wait for a billing clerk.

control.basis: Revenue recognition and cut-off (ASC 606, audited financial statements): invoices and revenue follow the shipment that transfers control

next.condition: clean invoice sent by EDI or email
clean invoice; customer requires portal submission

evidence.note: Invoice issued after fulfilment and booked subject to revenue recognition rules (wiki_o2c); PCF 9.2.2.2 to 9.2.2.4. Billing block and portal shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Clear billing block
steps.description: The billing clerk works the billing block list: confirms price overrides, adds freight not yet priced, enters a missing customer PO number, and applies sales tax where the customer's exemption certificate is missing or expired, then releases the invoice.

control.basis: State sales and use tax laws: tax is charged unless a valid exemption or resale certificate is on file

next.condition: released and sent by EDI or email

evidence.note: PCF 9.2.2.2 generate customer billing data. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Upload invoice to customer portal
steps.description: For customers that only accept invoices through their own supplier portal, the billing clerk logs in, re-keys or flips the invoice against the customer's PO, attaches the PDF, and fixes any portal rejection for PO or price mismatch.

error.defect_description: Portal rejects the invoice for a PO or price mismatch and nobody notices

evidence.note: Customer AP portals named as a remittance and invoicing channel. Re-keying times are author estimates.

steps.name: Customer processes and pays invoice
steps.description: The customer's AP team receives, matches and approves the invoice in their own process and pays on their payment run, usually near or after the due date on net 30 terms. Many invoices are not paid by the due date.
outputs: payment or no payment at due date

next.condition: paid by or shortly after the due date

evidence.note: Late payments affected 50 percent of the value of US B2B credit sales in 2021 (atradius_usmca2021); this file uses 48 percent of invoices. The payment wait is set so the order-to-cash median sits near the APQC median DSO of 38 days plus order-to-invoice time (cfo_dso), with net 30 terms as an author assumption; large US companies have higher DSO (cfo_2022).

steps.name: Send dunning reminder
steps.description: The weekly dunning run sends a past-due reminder or statement by email to the customer's AP contact for invoices past due beyond a short grace period.

evidence.note: Debt pursued through dunning cycles (wiki_o2c). Timing and response share are author estimates.

steps.name: Contact customer about overdue invoice
steps.description: The collector works a call list sorted by amount and age, calls or emails the customer's AP contact, and records the outcome: a promise to pay, a dispute, an invoice the customer never received, or no answer. Contacts usually cover several invoices of one customer at once.
outputs: promise to pay, dispute or resend request

next.condition: invoice not received or not in customer's system

evidence.note: PCF 9.2.4.3 correspond and negotiate with delinquent accounts. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Escalate seriously overdue account
steps.description: The credit manager reviews accounts far past due, puts the account on credit hold, sends a final demand, negotiates a payment plan, or places the debt with a collection agency and proposes a write-off.
outputs: payment plan, agency placement or write-off proposal

next.condition: placed with agency and written off

evidence.note: PCF 9.2.4.5 to 9.2.4.7; write-offs reported by atradius_usmca2021; APQC uncollectible balances 0.55 to 0.81 percent of revenue (cfo_baddebt). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Wait for promised payment
steps.description: After a promise to pay, a resent invoice or an agreed plan, the case waits for the customer's next payment run. Broken promises go back to the collector.

evidence.note: Customer payment run timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Receive payment and auto-match
steps.description: The bank's lockbox and ACH files arrive each morning; the ERP imports them and matches each payment to open invoices by invoice number and amount from the remittance. Payments without readable remittance, or that do not equal the invoices, go to the cash application queue.
outputs: posted cash or unapplied cash item

next.condition: needs manual match or short payment

evidence.note: Cash application flow from emagia_cashapp; 57 percent of organisations had some cash application automation by 2025 (emagia_sson). The 55 percent auto-match rate for 2019 to 2022 is an author estimate.

steps.name: Apply cash manually
steps.description: The cash application specialist finds the remittance in the AR mailbox, a customer portal or the check image, identifies the invoices paid, applies the payment, takes allowed early-payment discounts, and codes any short payment as a deduction with a reason code.

error.defect_description: Payment applied to the wrong invoice or customer

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting (SOX 404 for public issuers): staff who apply cash cannot issue credit memos or approve write-offs

next.condition: short payment coded as a deduction

evidence.note: Remittance capture, matching and deduction coding from emagia_cashapp; PCF 9.2.3.3 apply cash remittances. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Research deduction or dispute
steps.description: The deductions analyst pulls the invoice, the customer's claim, the proof of delivery, the price agreement and any promotion terms, decides whether the claim is valid, and asks the customer for backup when it is missing. Backlogs mean many items wait weeks.

error.defect_description: Valid claim denied or invalid claim accepted

next.condition: valid: pricing error, shortage, damage or agreed allowance

evidence.note: PCF 9.2.5.2 analyze adjustments; evidence gathering from emagia_disputes; APQC adjustment resolution takes seven days or fewer for the fastest quarter and three weeks or more for the slowest (cfo_billing_adj). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Sales validates claim
steps.description: The sales rep receives the analyst's email about a pricing, allowance or return claim, checks what was agreed with the customer, and replies whether to accept or deny it. Replies are often slow because sales treats it as low priority.

error.defect_description: Accepts a claim to protect the relationship without documenting why

evidence.note: PCF 9.2.5.4 discuss resolution with internal parties. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Pursue invalid deduction with customer
steps.description: The deductions analyst sends the customer a denial with the proof of delivery or agreement and asks for repayment, or issues a chargeback invoice, and follows up when the customer does not respond.

next.condition: small balance or partial agreement; credit or write-off

evidence.note: PCF 9.2.5.3 correspond and negotiate with customer; 9.2.5.5 prepare chargeback invoices. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Approve credit memo or write-off
steps.description: The credit manager reviews the proposed credit memo or write-off with its reason code and support, and approves it within their limit or sends it back. Larger amounts go to the controller.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting (SOX 404 for public issuers): credit memos and write-offs approved within limits by someone independent of cash application and billing

evidence.note: PCF 9.2.4.5 process adjustments and write off balances. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Issue credit memo and close item
steps.description: The billing clerk creates the approved credit memo or write-off entry in the ERP, nets it against the open deduction, and sends the credit memo to the customer so the item closes.

error.defect_description: Credit memo keyed for the wrong amount

evidence.note: PCF 9.2.5.6 process related entries. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Resend invoice copy
steps.description: When the customer says it never received the invoice or cannot find it in its system, the collector resends the invoice and proof of delivery by email or through the customer's portal and notes the new expected payment date.

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for a mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

exceptions.name: Price mismatch at order entry
exceptions.description: The customer's PO price differs from the contract or list price; sales confirms or the customer corrects the order.

exceptions.name: Credit block
exceptions.description: The order exceeds the limit or the customer is past due; the analyst releases, holds for payment or escalates.

exceptions.name: New customer credit setup
exceptions.description: No credit account exists; the analyst collects the application, references and credit report and the manager approves a limit.

exceptions.name: Backorder
exceptions.description: Stock is short at picking; customer service agrees a partial shipment or a wait for stock.

exceptions.name: Billing block or portal submission
exceptions.description: The invoice needs a billing clerk to fix price, freight, PO number or tax, or must be keyed into the customer's portal.

exceptions.name: Late payment and collections
exceptions.description: The invoice is not paid at the due date; dunning, collector calls, resends and escalation follow.

exceptions.name: Deduction or dispute
exceptions.description: The customer short-pays or disputes; the analyst researches, sales validates, and the item closes by credit memo, repayment or write-off.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from order receipt to cash applied

evidence.note: Derived, not measured: APQC cross-industry median DSO of 38 days (cfo_dso) plus about four days from order to invoice. For the 1,000 largest US non-financial companies DSO averaged 40.6 days with a median of 48.7 days in 2021 (cfo_2022). DSO is a balance measure, not the payment time of one invoice (wiki_dso). p90 reflects the half of B2B credit sales paid late (atradius_usmca2021) and is an author estimate.

benchmarks.population: APQC Customer Credit and Invoicing benchmarking (as cited)

evidence.note: Covers APQC process accounts receivable (receiving and applying cash, AR reporting); at $480 million revenue the median is about $2.70 per order, close to the cash application labour in this workflow of about $2 per order.

benchmarks.population: 1,000 largest non-financial US companies (Hackett Group Working Capital Survey)
US companies surveyed by Atradius, Q2 2021
US companies surveyed by Atradius, Q2 2021

evidence.note: A survey figure from a pandemic year; much higher than the write-off share in this workflow (about 0.8 percent) and than APQC uncollectible balances (cfo_baddebt).

benchmarks.population: US industries surveyed by Atradius, Q2 2021
SSON Future of O2C 2025 respondents (as cited)

evidence.note: Later than the reference period; the 2019 to 2022 share was probably lower.

pain_points.description: Customers pay late and collectors spend their time chasing invoices the customer never received, could not match in its portal, or forgot, rather than true credit risks.

evidence.note: Late payment share from Atradius; the mix of causes is an author estimate.

pain_points.description: Electronic payments arrive without remittance, so a large share of receipts need manual matching from emails and customer portals and cash sits unapplied.
Deductions pile up because research needs proof of delivery, pricing agreements and slow replies from sales, and small items are written off rather than pursued.
Credit blocks on good customers delay shipments while analysts check aging and payments in transit.
Order entry re-keys emailed PDF purchase orders and invoices are re-keyed into customers' portals, creating errors that surface later as disputes.

evidence.note: Author's reading of common B2B practice in the period.

sources.title: Boosting efficiency in accounts receivable processing: Metric of the Month (citing APQC)
sources.supports: Total cost to process accounts receivable per $1,000 revenue: median $0.34, 25th percentile $0.18, 75th percentile $0.58; personnel is the largest cost.

sources.title: What is the order-to-cash (O2C) process?
sources.supports: Describes eight O2C steps: order management, credit management (check creditworthiness, set limits; manual reviews hold orders), fulfilment and shipping, invoicing, AR management, collections, dispute and deduction management, cash application and reconciliation.

sources.title: What is cash application?
sources.supports: Cash application steps: receive payment (lockbox, ACH, wire, card, portals), capture remittance (check stubs, bank files, emails, EDI 820, customer AP portals), identify customer, match to invoices, route short payments and deductions with reason codes, post and reconcile. Electronic payments arrive separately from remittance; unapplied cash causes.

sources.title: How to handle customer payment disputes faster
sources.supports: Dispute steps: acknowledge, collect evidence (invoices, delivery confirmations, correspondence), investigate root cause, propose and communicate resolution, escalate, document.

assumptions: General workflow for a US mid-size B2B manufacturer or distributor of about 2,000 employees; 5,000 orders a month (tier C).
One order is one shipment and one invoice; split shipments and multi-invoice payments are folded into the per-order times.
Loaded cost per hour = BLS May 2021 wage x 1.8 (benefits factor 1.43 from BLS ECEC December 2021, overhead factor 1.25 estimated).

Pick and pack labour is included as one physical step (s11) because the order cannot be invoiced without it; it accounts for about half of the hands-on time and can be removed if a separate fulfilment workflow covers it.

Net 30 terms are assumed. The customer payment wait (s17) is calibrated so that the simulated median order-to-cash time sits near the 2021 median DSO of large US companies; DSO is a balance measure, so this is an approximation.
The backorder loop re-uses the normal picking wait; a real wait for replenishment can be weeks, so backordered cases are understated.

The write-off share in this workflow (about 0.8 percent of orders) matches APQC uncollectible balances of 0.55 to 0.81 percent of revenue and is far below the Atradius survey figure of 8 percent of invoices written off, which is self-reported for a pandemic year.
Collector contacts usually cover several invoices of one customer; per-invoice touch times are the call time divided across those invoices.
External party steps (customer, bank) carry zero hands-on time.
The simulated p90 (about 65 days) is below the 80-day p90 estimate because triangular waits cap the slowest payers; real receivables have a long tail of invoices over 90 days.
Branch shares for credit blocks, billing blocks, auto-match and deductions are author estimates; no public event log for B2B order to cash was used.
